SEC-HSTS-001.title: Missing or Weak HSTS Header
SEC-HSTS-001.description: The Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header is missing or has insufficient max-age value. This leaves users vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks during the initial connection or after the HSTS period expires.
SEC-HSTS-001.impact: Attackers can intercept traffic, steal credentials, or inject malicious content via protocol downgrade attacks.
SEC-HSTS-001.remediation:
Add the following HTTP header to all HTTPS responses:

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

For Apache (.htaccess or httpd.conf):
Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"

For Nginx:
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;

For application code (Express/Node.js):
app.use(helmet.hsts({ maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true, preload: true }));

SEC-FRAME-001.title: Missing Clickjacking Protection
SEC-FRAME-001.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive is present, leaving the site vulnerable to clickjacking attacks.
SEC-FRAME-001.impact: Attackers can embed your site in a malicious iframe and trick users into performing unintended actions.
SEC-FRAME-001.remediation:
Option 1 - Use X-Frame-Options:
X-Frame-Options: DENY

Or if you need to allow same-origin framing:
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN

Option 2 - Use Content-Security-Policy (preferred):
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

For Apache:
Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"

For Nginx:
add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;

For Express/Node.js:
app.use(helmet.frameguard({ action: 'deny' }));

SEC-XCTO-001.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
SEC-XCTO-001.description: The X-Content-Type-Options header is not set, allowing browsers to MIME-sniff content types, which can lead to security vulnerabilities.
SEC-XCTO-001.impact: Browsers may misinterpret file types, potentially executing malicious scripts disguised as other content types.
SEC-XCTO-001.remediation:
Add the following header to all responses:
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

For Apache:
Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"

For Nginx:
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;

For Express/Node.js:
app.use(helmet.noSniff());

SEC-RP-001.title: Missing or Weak Referrer-Policy
SEC-RP-001.description: The Referrer-Policy header is missing or uses a permissive policy, potentially leaking sensitive information in referrer headers.
SEC-RP-001.impact: URLs containing session tokens, user IDs, or other sensitive data may be leaked to third-party sites.
SEC-RP-001.remediation:
Add a restrictive Referrer-Policy header:
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

Or for maximum privacy:
Referrer-Policy: no-referrer

For Apache:
Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

For Nginx:
add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;

For Express/Node.js:
app.use(helmet.referrerPolicy({ policy: 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' }));

SEC-HTTPS-001.title: HTTP Not Redirecting to HTTPS
SEC-HTTPS-001.description: The HTTP version of the site does not properly redirect to HTTPS, allowing insecure connections.
SEC-HTTPS-001.impact: Sensitive data may be transmitted unencrypted, vulnerable to interception and manipulation.

SEC-TLS-001.title: Outdated TLS Version
SEC-TLS-001.description: The server is using TLS 1.0 or 1.1, which are deprecated and have known vulnerabilities.
SEC-TLS-001.impact: Connections may be vulnerable to attacks like POODLE, BEAST, and other protocol-level exploits.
SEC-TLS-001.remediation:
Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Enable TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only.

For Apache (SSLProtocol directive):
SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3

For Nginx:
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;

SEC-COOKIE-001.title: Missing Secure Flag on Cookie
SEC-COOKIE-001.description: Session or authentication cookies are missing the Secure flag, allowing them to be transmitted over unencrypted connections.
SEC-COOKIE-001.impact: Cookies may be intercepted over HTTP connections, leading to session hijacking.
SEC-COOKIE-001.remediation:
Add the Secure flag to all cookies:
Set-Cookie: sessionid=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

For application code:
- PHP: session.cookie_secure = 1
- Express: cookie: { secure: true }
- Django: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True

SEC-COOKIE-002.title: Missing HttpOnly Flag on Cookie
SEC-COOKIE-002.description: Cookies are missing the HttpOnly flag, making them accessible to JavaScript and vulnerable to XSS attacks.
SEC-COOKIE-002.impact: Attackers can steal session cookies via cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
SEC-COOKIE-002.remediation:
Add the HttpOnly flag to all cookies:
Set-Cookie: sessionid=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

For application code:
- PHP: session.cookie_httponly = 1
- Express: cookie: { httpOnly: true }
- Django: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True

SEC-COOKIE-003.title: Missing SameSite Attribute on Cookie
SEC-COOKIE-003.description: Cookies lack the SameSite attribute, leaving them vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) attacks.
SEC-COOKIE-003.impact: Attackers can perform actions on behalf of authenticated users by tricking them into visiting malicious sites.
SEC-COOKIE-003.remediation:
Add the SameSite attribute to cookies:
Set-Cookie: sessionid=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

Or use SameSite=Lax for better compatibility:
Set-Cookie: sessionid=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax

For application code:
- Express: cookie: { sameSite: 'strict' }
- Django: SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = 'Strict'

SEC-REDIR-001.title: HTTP Redirect Should Use 308 Instead of 301
SEC-REDIR-001.description: The HTTP to HTTPS redirect uses 301 (Moved Permanently) instead of 308 (Permanent Redirect). While both work, 308 preserves the request method and body.
SEC-REDIR-001.impact: POST requests may be converted to GET during redirect, though this is rare in practice for this specific scenario.
SEC-REDIR-001.remediation:
Configure your web server to use 308 redirects:

For Apache:
Redirect 308 / https://example.com/

For Nginx:
return 308 https://$server_name$request_uri;

SEC-REDIR-002.title: Temporary HTTP Redirect Used
SEC-REDIR-002.description: The HTTP to HTTPS redirect uses a temporary redirect (302/307) instead of a permanent one (301/308), which is less secure and inefficient.
SEC-REDIR-002.impact: Browsers won't cache the redirect, requiring an insecure HTTP request on every visit. Search engines won't transfer SEO value.
SEC-REDIR-002.remediation:
Change to a permanent redirect:

For Apache:
Redirect 308 / https://example.com/

For Nginx:
return 308 https://$server_name$request_uri;

SEC-REDIR-003.title: HTTP Redirects to Non-HTTPS URL
SEC-REDIR-003.description: The HTTP version redirects to a non-HTTPS URL, defeating the purpose of transport security.
SEC-REDIR-003.impact: Traffic remains unencrypted and vulnerable to interception.
SEC-REDIR-003.remediation:
Ensure all HTTP traffic redirects to HTTPS URLs only:

For Apache:
RewriteEngine On
RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://%{HTTP_HOST}/$1 [R=308,L]

For Nginx:
return 308 https://$server_name$request_uri;

SEC-REDIR-004.title: No HTTPS Redirect Configured
SEC-REDIR-004.description: HTTP requests do not redirect to HTTPS, allowing unencrypted connections.
SEC-REDIR-004.impact: Users can access the site over HTTP, exposing their data to interception and manipulation.

SEC-HSTS-002.title: HSTS Missing includeSubDomains or preload
SEC-HSTS-002.description: The HSTS header is present but missing recommended directives (includeSubDomains, preload) for comprehensive protection.
SEC-HSTS-002.impact: Subdomains may not be protected by HSTS, and the domain cannot be included in browser HSTS preload lists.
SEC-HSTS-002.remediation:
Enhance the HSTS header:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

For Apache:
Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"

For Nginx:
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;

Note: Before adding 'preload', submit your domain to https://hstspreload.org/

SEC-HSTS-003.title: HSTS Configuration Issues
SEC-HSTS-003.description: The HSTS header has multiple configuration issues (low max-age, missing directives).
SEC-HSTS-003.impact: Incomplete HSTS protection leaves gaps for man-in-the-middle attacks.
SEC-HSTS-003.remediation:
Fix all HSTS configuration issues:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

Ensure:
- max-age is at least 31536000 (1 year)
- includeSubDomains is present
- preload is added (optional but recommended)

For Apache:
Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"

For Nginx:
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;

SEC-CSP-001.title: Missing Content Security Policy
SEC-CSP-001.description: No Content-Security-Policy header is present, leaving the site vulnerable to XSS and data injection attacks.
SEC-CSP-001.impact: Attackers can inject and execute malicious scripts, steal data, or deface the website.
SEC-CSP-001.remediation:
Implement a Content Security Policy:

Basic starting policy:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

For Apache:
Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'"

For Nginx:
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'" always;

For Express/Node.js:
app.use(helmet.contentSecurityPolicy({ directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"], scriptSrc: ["'self'"] }}));

SEC-CSP-002.title: Weak Content Security Policy
SEC-CSP-002.description: The CSP contains one risky directive that weakens its effectiveness.
SEC-CSP-002.impact: The policy provides some XSS protection but has gaps that could be exploited.
SEC-CSP-002.remediation:
Strengthen your CSP by removing risky directives:

1. Remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src and style-src
2. Remove 'unsafe-eval' from script-src
3. Avoid wildcards (*) in script-src
4. Remove data: URIs from script-src
5. Add a default-src fallback

Better policy:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{random}'; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'

Implement nonce-based CSP for inline scripts instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

SEC-CSP-003.title: Multiple CSP Weaknesses Detected
SEC-CSP-003.description: The Content Security Policy has multiple risky directives that significantly weaken its protection.
SEC-CSP-003.impact: The policy may not effectively prevent XSS attacks due to permissive directives.
SEC-CSP-003.remediation:
Rebuild your CSP with a strict baseline:

Strict CSP example:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{random}'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'

Key principles:
1. Start with default-src 'none' or 'self'
2. Never use 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' in script-src
3. Avoid wildcards (*)
4. Use nonces or hashes for required inline scripts
5. Include frame-ancestors directive

Test with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.

SEC-INFO-001.title: Server Information Leakage
SEC-INFO-001.description: HTTP headers expose server software versions and framework details that aid attackers in reconnaissance.
SEC-INFO-001.impact: Attackers can identify specific software versions and target known vulnerabilities more effectively.
SEC-INFO-001.remediation:
Remove or obfuscate identifying headers:

For Apache:
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
Header always unset X-Powered-By
Header always unset X-AspNet-Version
Header always unset X-AspNetMvc-Version

For Nginx:
server_tokens off;
more_clear_headers Server;
more_clear_headers X-Powered-By;

For Express/Node.js:
app.disable('x-powered-by');

For ASP.NET (web.config):
<httpRuntime enableVersionHeader="false" />
<system.webServer>
  <httpProtocol>
    <customHeaders>
      <remove name="X-Powered-By" />
      <remove name="X-AspNet-Version" />
      <remove name="X-AspNetMvc-Version" />
    </customHeaders>
  </httpProtocol>
</system.webServer>

SEC-CERT-001.title: Certificate Retrieval Failed
SEC-CERT-001.description: Unable to retrieve the SSL/TLS certificate for validation.
SEC-CERT-001.impact: Cannot verify the security of the connection; the site may not be using HTTPS properly.
SEC-CERT-001.remediation:
Ensure the site has a valid SSL/TLS certificate installed:

1. Obtain a certificate from a trusted CA (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.)
2. Install the certificate on your web server
3. Configure HTTPS properly

For Let's Encrypt:
sudo certbot --nginx -d example.com

For Apache with existing certificate:
SSLCertificateFile /path/to/certificate.crt
SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/private.key
SSLCertificateChainFile /path/to/chain.crt

SEC-CERT-002.title: Certificate Expiry Parse Error
SEC-CERT-002.description: The certificate was retrieved but the expiry date could not be parsed.
SEC-CERT-002.impact: Cannot determine if the certificate is still valid.
SEC-CERT-002.remediation:
Check your certificate manually:

openssl s_client -servername example.com -connect example.com:443 < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

If the certificate appears malformed, regenerate it.

SEC-CERT-003.title: Certificate Date Format Error
SEC-CERT-003.description: The certificate expiry date is in an unrecognized format.
SEC-CERT-003.impact: Automated checking cannot determine validity period.
SEC-CERT-003.remediation: Check certificate validity manually and consider regenerating if format is non-standard.

SEC-CERT-004.title: Certificate Expired
SEC-CERT-004.description: The SSL/TLS certificate has expired and is no longer valid.
SEC-CERT-004.impact: Browsers will warn users and block access. The connection is untrusted and potentially vulnerable.
SEC-CERT-004.remediation:
Renew your certificate immediately:

For Let's Encrypt:
sudo certbot renew

For other providers:
1. Request a new certificate from your CA
2. Install the renewed certificate
3. Restart your web server

Consider setting up automatic renewal.

SEC-CERT-005.title: Certificate Expiring Soon (< 7 Days)
SEC-CERT-005.description: The SSL/TLS certificate will expire in less than 7 days.
SEC-CERT-005.impact: Imminent expiry will cause browsers to warn users and may result in service disruption.
SEC-CERT-005.remediation:
Renew your certificate urgently:

For Let's Encrypt:
sudo certbot renew

For manual certificates:
1. Generate or request a new certificate
2. Install it before expiration
3. Set up automated renewal to prevent future issues

SEC-CERT-006.title: Certificate Expiring Within 30 Days
SEC-CERT-006.description: The SSL/TLS certificate will expire in less than 30 days.
SEC-CERT-006.impact: Certificate will expire soon. Plan renewal to avoid service disruption.
SEC-CERT-006.remediation:
Plan to renew your certificate:

For Let's Encrypt (with auto-renewal):
sudo certbot renew --dry-run

If auto-renewal isn't working, renew manually:
sudo certbot renew

For other providers, request renewal and schedule installation.

SEC-FILES-001.title: Sensitive File Exposed
SEC-FILES-001.description: A sensitive file (configuration, backup, or version control file) is publicly accessible.
SEC-FILES-001.impact: Exposed files may contain credentials, API keys, source code, or other sensitive information that aids attackers.

SEC-FILES-002.title: Multiple Sensitive Files Exposed
SEC-FILES-002.description: Multiple sensitive files and directories are publicly accessible, indicating poor deployment practices.
SEC-FILES-002.impact: Widespread exposure of sensitive files creates multiple attack vectors and may expose credentials, source code, or database contents.
SEC-FILES-002.remediation:
Immediately restrict access to all sensitive files:

For Apache (.htaccess):
# Block sensitive files
<FilesMatch "^\.(htaccess|htpasswd|env|git)">
    Require all denied
</FilesMatch>
<FilesMatch "\.(sql|zip|tar\.gz|bak|config|log)$">
    Require all denied
</FilesMatch>

For Nginx:
location ~ /\.(git|env|htaccess|htpasswd) {
    deny all;
}
location ~ \.(sql|zip|tar\.gz|bak|config|log)$ {
    deny all;
}

Immediate actions:
1. Remove .git directories from production
2. Move .env files outside webroot
3. Delete all backup files (.sql, .zip, .bak)
4. Review and clean deployment process
5. Never commit sensitive files to version control

SEC-ADMIN-001.title: Admin Path Publicly Accessible
SEC-ADMIN-001.description: An administrative interface or sensitive debug endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.
SEC-ADMIN-001.impact: Attackers can access administrative functions, potentially gaining full control of the application.
SEC-ADMIN-001.remediation:
Restrict access to admin interfaces:

For Apache (.htaccess in /admin):
Require ip 192.168.1.0/24
# Or require authentication:
AuthType Basic
AuthName "Admin Access"
AuthUserFile /path/to/.htpasswd
Require valid-user

For Nginx:
location /admin {
    allow 192.168.1.0/24;
    deny all;
    # Or use auth_basic
}

Best practices:
1. Use IP whitelisting for admin areas
2. Require strong authentication (MFA)
3. Use non-standard admin paths
4. Disable debug endpoints in production
5. Monitor access logs for admin paths

SEC-ADMIN-002.title: Multiple Admin Paths Exposed
SEC-ADMIN-002.description: Multiple administrative interfaces or debug endpoints are publicly accessible.
SEC-ADMIN-002.impact: Widespread exposure of administrative functions creates severe security risks including complete system compromise.
SEC-ADMIN-002.remediation:
Immediately lock down all admin interfaces:

For Apache:
<LocationMatch "/(admin|phpmyadmin|server-status|actuator)">
    Require ip 192.168.1.0/24
    # Or require authentication:
    AuthType Basic
    AuthName "Restricted"
    AuthUserFile /path/to/.htpasswd
    Require valid-user
</LocationMatch>

For Nginx:
location ~ ^/(admin|phpmyadmin|server-status|actuator) {
    allow 192.168.1.0/24;
    deny all;
}

Urgent actions:
1. Immediately block public access to all admin paths
2. Review server configuration for debug modes
3. Disable server-status, server-info modules
4. Remove or protect PHPMyAdmin, actuator endpoints
5. Audit all access logs for admin paths
6. Consider using VPN for admin access

SEC-TLS-002.title: TLS 1.3 Not Supported
SEC-TLS-002.description: The server only supports TLS 1.2 but not TLS 1.3, the latest and most secure version.
SEC-TLS-002.impact: Missing improved security and performance benefits of TLS 1.3.
SEC-TLS-002.remediation:
Enable TLS 1.3 support:

For Apache:
SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3

For Nginx:
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;

Note: Ensure your OpenSSL version supports TLS 1.3 (OpenSSL 1.1.1+).

SEC-TLS-003.title: No Modern TLS Protocols Detected
SEC-TLS-003.description: Unable to detect TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 support on the server.
SEC-TLS-003.impact: Server may not support modern secure protocols, leaving connections vulnerable.
SEC-TLS-003.remediation:
Ensure TLS 1.2 and 1.3 are enabled:

For Apache:
SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3
SSLCipherSuite HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5

For Nginx:
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_ciphers HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5;

Verify:
openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -tls1_2

SEC-HEADERS-001.title: Missing Modern Security Header
SEC-HEADERS-001.description: One modern security header (Permissions-Policy, COOP, COEP, or CORP) is missing.
SEC-HEADERS-001.impact: Missing defense-in-depth protection against certain browser-based attacks.
SEC-HEADERS-001.remediation:
Add the missing header:

Permissions-Policy:
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()

Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy:
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy:
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy:
Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin

For Nginx:
add_header Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()" always;
add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin" always;

SEC-HEADERS-002.title: Multiple Modern Security Headers Missing
SEC-HEADERS-002.description: Two or more modern security headers are missing from the response.

SEC-HEADERS-003.title: Most Modern Security Headers Missing
SEC-HEADERS-003.description: Three or more modern security headers are missing, indicating lack of modern browser protections.
SEC-HEADERS-003.impact: Significant gaps in defense-in-depth protection against modern browser-based attacks.

SEC-CORS-001.title: CORS Allows Any Origin with Credentials
SEC-CORS-001.description: The most dangerous CORS misconfiguration: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
SEC-CORS-001.impact: Any malicious website can make authenticated requests to your API and steal user data.
SEC-CORS-001.remediation:
IMMEDIATELY fix this critical misconfiguration:

Option 1 - Remove credentials:
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: false

Option 2 - Restrict origin (RECOMMENDED):
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://trusted-domain.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

For Express:
app.use(cors({
  origin: 'https://trusted-domain.com',
  credentials: true
}));

NEVER use:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

SEC-CORS-002.title: CORS Misconfiguration Detected
SEC-CORS-002.description: CORS is configured in a way that may expose the application to attacks.
SEC-CORS-002.impact: Attackers may be able to make unauthorized cross-origin requests or steal sensitive data.

SEC-DIRLISTING-001.title: Directory Listing Enabled
SEC-DIRLISTING-001.description: One or more directories have directory listing enabled, exposing file structure.
SEC-DIRLISTING-001.impact: Attackers can discover files, analyze application structure, and find sensitive files more easily.
SEC-DIRLISTING-001.remediation:
Disable directory listing:

For Apache (.htaccess or httpd.conf):
Options -Indexes

For Nginx:
autoindex off;

For IIS (web.config):
<configuration>
  <system.webServer>
    <directoryBrowse enabled="false" />
  </system.webServer>
</configuration>

Best practices:
1. Place an index file in every directory
2. Disable at server level, not just per-directory
3. Review exposed files and remove sensitive ones

SEC-DIRLISTING-002.title: Multiple Directories with Listing Enabled
SEC-DIRLISTING-002.description: Multiple directories have directory listing enabled across the application.
SEC-DIRLISTING-002.impact: Widespread exposure of file structure aids attackers in reconnaissance and finding vulnerabilities.
SEC-DIRLISTING-002.remediation:
Immediately disable directory listing globally:

For Apache (httpd.conf):
<Directory /var/www>
    Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
</Directory>

For Nginx (nginx.conf):
http {
    autoindex off;
}

For IIS (applicationHost.config):
<system.webServer>
  <directoryBrowse enabled="false" />
</system.webServer>

Urgent actions:
1. Disable globally at server level
2. Audit all exposed directories
3. Remove any sensitive files found
4. Add index.html to all public directories
5. Review deployment process to prevent recurrence

SEC-API-001.title: Open API Endpoint Detected
SEC-API-001.description: An API endpoint is accessible without authentication.
SEC-API-001.impact: Unauthorized users can access API functionality and potentially sensitive data.

SEC-API-002.title: Multiple Open API Endpoints
SEC-API-002.description: Multiple API endpoints are accessible without authentication.
SEC-API-002.impact: Widespread API exposure allows unauthorized access to application functionality and data.

SEC-ERROR-001.title: Verbose Error Pages Detected
SEC-ERROR-001.description: Error pages expose sensitive information such as stack traces, file paths, or framework details.
SEC-ERROR-001.impact: Information disclosure aids attackers in identifying vulnerabilities and planning attacks.
SEC-ERROR-001.remediation:
Disable detailed error messages in production:

For PHP (php.ini):
display_errors = Off
log_errors = On
error_log = /var/log/php_errors.log

For Node.js/Express:
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') {
  app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' });
  });
}

For Django (settings.py):
DEBUG = False
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['yourdomain.com']

For ASP.NET (web.config):
<system.web>
  <customErrors mode="On" defaultRedirect="~/Error">
    <error statusCode="404" redirect="~/Error/NotFound" />
    <error statusCode="500" redirect="~/Error/ServerError" />
  </customErrors>
</system.web>

Best practices:
1. Log errors server-side
2. Show generic error messages to users
3. Never expose stack traces
4. Hide framework versions
5. Remove debug endpoints in production

SEC-ERROR-002.title: Multiple Verbose Error Patterns Detected
SEC-ERROR-002.description: Error pages expose multiple types of sensitive information including stack traces, file paths, and framework details.
SEC-ERROR-002.impact: Extensive information disclosure significantly aids attackers in identifying vulnerabilities.
SEC-ERROR-002.remediation:
Immediately disable all verbose error output:

1. Set application to production mode
2. Disable debug mode completely
3. Configure custom error pages
4. Enable comprehensive server-side logging

Example production configuration:

PHP:
display_errors = Off
display_startup_errors = Off
log_errors = On
error_reporting = E_ALL & ~E_DEPRECATED & ~E_STRICT

Node.js:
process.env.NODE_ENV = 'production';
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  console.error(err.stack); // Log server-side only
  res.status(500).send('Server Error');
});

Django:
DEBUG = False
SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True

Urgent actions:
1. Verify production mode is enabled
2. Test error pages with non-sensitive information
3. Review server logs for errors (don't expose to users)
4. Set up proper monitoring/alerting
5. Remove any debug endpoints or tools

SEC-CACHE-001.title: Missing Cache-Control on Sensitive Path
SEC-CACHE-001.description: A sensitive path (login, account, admin) does not have proper Cache-Control headers to prevent caching of sensitive data.
SEC-CACHE-001.impact: Sensitive information may be cached by browsers or intermediary proxies, potentially exposing user data.

SEC-CACHE-002.title: Multiple Sensitive Paths Without Cache-Control
SEC-CACHE-002.description: Multiple sensitive paths lack proper Cache-Control headers, creating widespread caching risks.
SEC-CACHE-002.impact: Widespread caching of sensitive data increases the risk of information disclosure through browser history or proxy caches.

SEC-ENUM-001.title: User Enumeration Vulnerability
SEC-ENUM-001.description: An endpoint allows user enumeration, enabling attackers to identify valid usernames or user IDs.
SEC-ENUM-001.impact: Attackers can harvest valid usernames to focus password attacks, phishing campaigns, or other targeted attacks.

SEC-ENUM-002.title: Multiple User Enumeration Vectors
SEC-ENUM-002.description: Multiple endpoints expose user enumeration capabilities, creating significant reconnaissance opportunities for attackers.
SEC-ENUM-002.impact: Widespread user enumeration enables large-scale credential attacks and targeted phishing campaigns.

SEC-SESS-001.title: Session Cookie Assigned Before Authentication
SEC-SESS-001.description: The application assigns a session cookie to unauthenticated requests. If the session ID is not regenerated after login, an attacker who plants a known session ID can hijack the authenticated session (session fixation).
SEC-SESS-001.impact: An attacker can pre-set a known session ID in the victim's browser, then hijack the authenticated session after the victim logs in.
SEC-SESS-001.remediation:
Regenerate session ID immediately after successful authentication:

PHP:
session_regenerate_id(true); // Call after successful login

Express/Node.js (express-session):
req.session.regenerate(function(err) {
  // store new user info in req.session
});

Django:
from django.contrib.auth import login
login(request, user) // Django auto-regenerates session on login

Spring Security (auto-handled):
http.sessionManagement()
    .sessionFixation().migrateSession(); // default behavior

Also ensure:
1. Session cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Strict/Lax
2. Invalidate old session on logout
3. Set short session timeouts
4. Bind sessions to IP/User-Agent where practical

SEC-SESS-002.title: Session Fixation with Missing Cookie Security Attributes
SEC-SESS-002.description: Pre-authentication session cookies lack Secure, HttpOnly, and/or SameSite attributes, compounding the session fixation risk.
SEC-SESS-002.impact: Combination of session fixation vectors with insecure cookie attributes significantly increases hijacking risk.
SEC-SESS-002.remediation:
Address both session fixation and cookie security:

1. Regenerate session ID on login (see SEC-SESS-001)

2. Set all cookie security attributes:
Set-Cookie: sessionid=<value>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/

PHP:
session_set_cookie_params([
    'secure' => true,
    'httponly' => true,
    'samesite' => 'Strict'
]);

Express:
app.use(session({
    secret: 'strong-secret',
    cookie: {
        secure: true,
        httpOnly: true,
        sameSite: 'strict',
        maxAge: 3600000
    },
    resave: false,
    saveUninitialized: false
}));

3. Never accept session IDs from URL parameters
4. Implement CSRF protection alongside session management

SEC-OCSP-001.title: OCSP Stapling Not Enabled
SEC-OCSP-001.description: The server does not staple an OCSP response to the TLS handshake, requiring clients to perform separate OCSP lookups to validate certificate revocation status. This reduces performance and privacy.
SEC-OCSP-001.impact: Without OCSP stapling, clients must query the CA's OCSP server directly, leaking browsing activity to the CA and adding latency. In OCSP soft-fail scenarios, revoked certificates may still be trusted.
SEC-OCSP-001.remediation:
Enable OCSP stapling on your web server:

Nginx:
ssl_stapling on;
ssl_stapling_verify on;
resolver 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4 valid=300s;
resolver_timeout 5s;
# Include full certificate chain:
ssl_certificate /path/to/fullchain.pem;

Apache:
SSLUseStapling on
SSLStaplingCache shmcb:/var/run/ocsp(128000)
SSLStaplingStapleMaxAge 3600

HAProxy:
# Use certbot/acme.sh for automatic OCSP stapling

Verify with:
echo '' | openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 -status 2>/dev/null | grep 'OCSP Response Status'

Requirements:
- Full certificate chain (not just leaf cert)
- Network access from server to CA OCSP responder
- Valid stapling cache configuration

SEC-OCSP-002.title: Certificate Revoked (OCSP Response)
SEC-OCSP-002.description: The OCSP response indicates the server's certificate has been revoked. Clients will receive security warnings or connection failures.
SEC-OCSP-002.impact: Revoked certificates should not be trusted. Browsers may block access or show severe warnings, breaking the site for all users.
SEC-OCSP-002.remediation:
Immediately replace the revoked certificate:

1. Obtain a new certificate from your CA or Let's Encrypt:
   certbot renew --force-renewal

2. Deploy the new certificate:
   - Update ssl_certificate and ssl_certificate_key in Nginx/Apache
   - Reload the web server: nginx -s reload / systemctl reload apache2

3. Verify the new certificate:
   echo '' | openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

4. Investigate why the certificate was revoked:
   - Private key compromise?
   - CA-initiated revocation?
   - Misissuance?

5. If private key was compromised, rotate all secrets and audit access logs

SEC-DNS-001.title: Missing DNS Security Records
SEC-DNS-001.description: One or more DNS security records (DNSSEC, SPF, DMARC, CAA) are missing or not properly configured, leaving the domain vulnerable to spoofing, impersonation, and unauthorized certificate issuance.
SEC-DNS-001.impact: Missing SPF/DMARC enables email spoofing from your domain. Missing CAA allows any CA to issue certificates. Missing DNSSEC enables DNS cache poisoning.
SEC-DNS-001.remediation:
Implement all DNS security records:

1. SPF record (TXT at root domain):
   v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all
   (replace with your actual mail provider)

2. DMARC record (TXT at _dmarc.yourdomain.com):
   v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com; fo=1
   Start with p=none, then p=quarantine, then p=reject

3. CAA record:
   0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
   0 issuewild ";"
   0 iodef "mailto:security@yourdomain.com"

4. DNSSEC: Enable via your DNS provider's control panel (varies by provider)
   - Cloudflare: Settings > DNSSEC (one-click)
   - Route53: Enable DNSSEC signing in hosted zone settings

Verify with:
   dig TXT yourdomain.com (SPF)
   dig TXT _dmarc.yourdomain.com (DMARC)
   dig CAA yourdomain.com
   dig DNSKEY yourdomain.com (DNSSEC)

SEC-DNS-002.title: Multiple Critical DNS Security Records Missing
SEC-DNS-002.description: Three or more DNS security records are absent, creating a broadly unsecured domain posture with multiple attack vectors.
SEC-DNS-002.impact: Comprehensive DNS security gaps expose the domain to DNS poisoning, email spoofing, certificate impersonation, and man-in-the-middle attacks.
SEC-DNS-002.remediation:
Treat DNS security as a priority remediation item:

Priority order:
1. DMARC p=reject (prevents email spoofing immediately)
2. SPF (defines authorized mail senders)
3. CAA (restricts certificate issuance)
4. DNSSEC (prevents DNS cache poisoning)

See SEC-DNS-001 for detailed implementation steps.

Additional hardening:
- DKIM: Generate keys for each mail service and publish DNS TXT records
- MTA-STS: Enforce TLS for inbound email
- TLSRPT: Monitor TLS failures
- Review all DNS records for dangling CNAMEs pointing to decommissioned services

SEC-GRAPHQL-001.title: GraphQL Introspection Enabled in Production
SEC-GRAPHQL-001.description: GraphQL introspection is enabled, allowing any user to query the full schema including all types, queries, mutations, and their arguments. This exposes the full API surface for reconnaissance.
SEC-GRAPHQL-001.impact: Attackers can enumerate the complete API schema to discover hidden endpoints, sensitive data types, and attack vectors without any authorization.

SEC-GRAPHQL-002.title: GraphQL Introspection and Playground Both Exposed
SEC-GRAPHQL-002.description: Both GraphQL introspection and the developer IDE (Playground/GraphiQL) are accessible in production, providing a complete interactive API exploration tool to attackers.
SEC-GRAPHQL-002.impact: Attackers have a fully interactive tool to explore, test, and attack the entire API without needing credentials or prior knowledge of the schema.

SEC-SUBDOMAIN-001.title: Sensitive Subdomains Exposed in Certificate Transparency Logs
SEC-SUBDOMAIN-001.description: Certificate transparency logs reveal subdomains with names suggesting sensitive internal environments (staging, dev, admin, vpn, etc.) that may not be intended for public exposure.
SEC-SUBDOMAIN-001.impact: Attackers can use CT log data to discover staging/dev environments that may have weaker security, older software versions, or debugging features enabled.
SEC-SUBDOMAIN-001.remediation:
Audit and secure exposed sensitive subdomains:

1. Review all CT log entries:
   curl 'https://crt.sh/?q=%.yourdomain.com&output=json' | jq '.[].name_value' | sort -u

2. For each sensitive subdomain:
   - Is it still in use? If not, remove DNS record and certificate
   - Does it require public access? If not, restrict to VPN/IP allowlist
   - Does it have authentication? Verify login is required
   - Is it running updated/patched software?

3. Restrict access to internal environments:
Nginx:
location / {
    allow 10.0.0.0/8;     # Corporate network
    allow 192.168.0.0/16;  # VPN
    deny all;
}

4. Remove subdomains you don't need:
   - Delete DNS A/CNAME records for decommissioned services
   - Revoke certificates for retired subdomains

5. Monitor CT logs continuously:
   - Use services like certspotter.com or Facebook CT Monitor
   - Set up alerts for new certificate issuance on your domain

SEC-REDIRECT-001.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability
SEC-REDIRECT-001.description: The application accepts a URL redirect parameter and redirects users to an externally controlled URL without validation. This can be used in phishing and SSO bypass attacks.
SEC-REDIRECT-001.impact: Attackers can craft URLs that appear to belong to your domain but redirect victims to malicious sites, bypassing browser warnings and facilitating credential theft.

SEC-REDIRECT-002.title: Multiple Open Redirect Parameters
SEC-REDIRECT-002.description: Multiple redirect parameters accept unvalidated external URLs, indicating a systematic lack of redirect validation across the application.
SEC-REDIRECT-002.impact: Multiple redirect vectors provide numerous phishing entry points and may indicate the vulnerability is embedded in shared redirect logic.

SEC-SRI-001.title: External Resources Loaded Without Subresource Integrity
SEC-SRI-001.description: External scripts or stylesheets are loaded without integrity attributes, meaning a compromised CDN or third-party host could serve malicious code that executes in users' browsers.
SEC-SRI-001.impact: If the CDN serving an external script is compromised, attackers can inject malicious JavaScript that executes on your site, leading to credential theft or data exfiltration.
SEC-SRI-001.remediation:
Add Subresource Integrity (SRI) to all external script and stylesheet tags:

1. Generate SRI hash:
   cat jquery.min.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A
   # Or use: https://www.srihash.org/

2. Add to HTML tag:
   <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jquery@3.6.0/dist/jquery.min.js"
           integrity="sha384-vtXRMe3mGCbOeY7l30aIg8H9p3GdeSe4IFlP6G8JMa7o7lXvnz3GFKzPxzJdPfGK"
           crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

   <link rel="stylesheet"
         href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.1.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
         integrity="sha384-1BmE4kWBq78iYhFldvKuhfTAU6auU8tT94WrHftjDbrCEXSU1oBoqyl2QvZ6jIW3"
         crossorigin="anonymous">

3. Automate SRI generation:
   npm install --save-dev webpack-subresource-integrity

4. Use Content-Security-Policy to enforce SRI:
   Content-Security-Policy: require-sri-for script style;

5. Self-host critical dependencies where possible to eliminate CDN risk

SEC-SRI-002.title: Multiple External Resources Without Subresource Integrity
SEC-SRI-002.description: Three or more external scripts or stylesheets lack SRI attributes, creating widespread supply chain risk across the page.
SEC-SRI-002.impact: A single CDN compromise could affect all unprotected external resources simultaneously, enabling large-scale malicious script injection.

SEC-WAF-001.title: No WAF or CDN Detected
SEC-WAF-001.description: The site does not appear to be protected by a Web Application Firewall (WAF) or CDN, meaning the origin server is directly exposed to the internet and potential attacks.
SEC-WAF-001.impact: Without a WAF, the origin is directly exposed to DDoS attacks, OWASP Top 10 exploits, bot traffic, and vulnerability scanning without any filtering layer.
SEC-WAF-001.remediation:
Deploy a WAF or CDN in front of the origin:

Option 1: Cloudflare (recommended for most sites):
1. Sign up at cloudflare.com
2. Change nameservers to Cloudflare NS
3. Enable WAF rules (Free tier includes basic rules)
4. Enable DDoS protection
5. Enable Bot Fight Mode

Option 2: AWS WAF + CloudFront:
1. Create CloudFront distribution pointing to origin
2. Attach AWS WAF WebACL with managed rule groups:
   - AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
   - AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
   - AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet

Option 3: nginx + ModSecurity (self-hosted):
apt install libnginx-mod-security2
# Enable OWASP Core Rule Set (CRS)

Minimum WAF rules to enable:
- SQLi protection
- XSS protection
- OWASP Top 10 rules
- Rate limiting / IP reputation
- Bot detection

After deploying WAF:
- Block direct origin IP access (only allow WAF IPs)
- Enable HTTPS (full strict mode in Cloudflare)
- Enable access logging for security monitoring

SEC-3P-001.title: Third-Party Scripts Loaded Without Inventory Review
SEC-3P-001.description: The page loads external third-party scripts from multiple domains. Each third-party script represents a supply chain risk — a compromise of any script host could inject malicious code into your site.
SEC-3P-001.impact: Third-party scripts execute with full page permissions and can exfiltrate form data, session tokens, and user PII if the script provider is compromised.
SEC-3P-001.remediation:
Inventory and control all third-party scripts:

1. Audit all loaded scripts:
   - Use browser DevTools > Network tab (filter by Script)
   - Use tools like RetireJS or Snyk for known-vulnerable libraries

2. Apply SRI to all external scripts (see SEC-SRI-001)

3. Implement a strict Content Security Policy:
   Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://trusted-cdn.com; default-src 'self';

4. Use a Tag Manager with governance:
   - Require approval for new tags
   - Set up tag timeouts/expiry
   - Monitor tag changes

5. Sandbox third-party scripts in iframes:
   <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src="...third-party..."></iframe>

6. Self-host critical dependencies:
   npm install && vendor the script locally

7. Perform regular supply chain audits:
   npm audit
   npx retiring

8. Monitor for unexpected new script additions using CSP reporting

SEC-3P-002.title: High-Risk Advertising or Tracking Scripts Detected
SEC-3P-002.description: The page loads advertising, analytics, or tracking scripts from high-risk third-party domains. These scripts typically have broad data collection capabilities and are frequent targets for malvertising attacks.
SEC-3P-002.impact: Advertising networks have been used in malvertising campaigns to deliver malware. Tracking scripts can exfiltrate user data and session information. Any compromised ad/tracking provider can execute arbitrary JS on your site.
SEC-3P-002.remediation:
Minimize and control advertising/tracking scripts:

1. Evaluate necessity of each tracking/ad SDK:
   - Is it actively used? When was ROI last measured?
   - Can functionality be replaced with a privacy-respecting alternative?

2. Load ad scripts asynchronously and in sandboxed contexts:
   <script async src="..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

3. Use a CSP to restrict script sources:
   Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://googletagmanager.com; ...

4. Apply SRI hashes where possible (some ad scripts change frequently)

5. Implement Subresource Integrity checking:
   npm install --save-dev csp-audit

6. For GDPR/CCPA compliance:
   - Implement consent management (don't load tracking before consent)
   - Use server-side tagging to reduce client-side exposure
   - Audit data sent to third parties

7. Monitor for unauthorized new tracking domains:
   Set up CSP report-to endpoint to detect policy violations

SEC-CLOUD-001.title: Cloud Storage Bucket Exists But Access Restricted
SEC-CLOUD-001.description: A cloud storage bucket matching the domain name was discovered but returned a 403 Forbidden response. While not publicly readable, the bucket exists and may be misconfigured if access controls are ever changed.
SEC-CLOUD-001.impact: A 403 confirms bucket existence, allowing attackers to monitor for permission changes. Historical misconfiguration, insecure bucket policies, or ACL changes could expose sensitive data.
SEC-CLOUD-001.remediation:
Verify and harden cloud storage bucket configuration:

AWS S3:
1. Enable S3 Block Public Access at account level:
   aws s3control put-public-access-block \
     --account-id 123456789 \
     --public-access-block-configuration 'BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true'

2. Review bucket policy:
   aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket your-bucket-name

3. Enable S3 Access Logging:
   aws s3api put-bucket-logging ...

4. Enable versioning and MFA delete for sensitive buckets

GCS:
1. Remove allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers from bucket IAM
2. Enable uniform bucket-level access
3. Enable Cloud Audit Logs

Azure Blob:
1. Set container access level to Private
2. Enable soft delete and versioning
3. Use Private Endpoints to restrict network access

General best practices:
- Least privilege: only grant the minimum required permissions
- Enable access logging on all buckets
- Use bucket lifecycle policies to expire old data
- Encrypt sensitive data at rest

SEC-CLOUD-002.title: Public Cloud Storage Bucket Exposed
SEC-CLOUD-002.description: A publicly accessible cloud storage bucket matching the target domain was found. Files in this bucket are readable by anyone on the internet.
SEC-CLOUD-002.impact: Exposed buckets can contain database backups, user uploads, configuration files with credentials, logs, PII, and source code — all accessible without authentication.
SEC-CLOUD-002.remediation:
IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED:

1. Disable public access immediately:

AWS S3:
# Block all public access:
aws s3api put-public-access-block \
  --bucket YOUR-BUCKET-NAME \
  --public-access-block-configuration 'BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true'

# Remove bucket policy if overly permissive:
aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket YOUR-BUCKET-NAME

GCS:
gcloud storage buckets update gs://YOUR-BUCKET --no-public-access-prevention=false
# Remove allUsers IAM binding:
gcloud storage buckets remove-iam-policy-binding gs://YOUR-BUCKET --member=allUsers --role=roles/storage.objectViewer

Azure Blob:
az storage container set-permission --name YOUR-CONTAINER --public-access off

2. Audit bucket contents:
   aws s3 ls s3://YOUR-BUCKET --recursive | head -100
   # Look for: .env, *.sql, *.bak, config*, credentials*, private*

3. If sensitive data was exposed:
   - Notify affected users per breach notification laws (GDPR, CCPA)
   - Rotate any exposed credentials IMMEDIATELY
   - Review access logs for evidence of data exfiltration
   - File incident report

4. Prevent recurrence:
   - Enable AWS Config rule: s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited
   - Set up CloudTrail + CloudWatch alarms for ACL changes
   - Use AWS Security Hub / GCP Security Command Center
